proposals.expected_failure_mode: Delay and waning-immunity effects can be confounded, yielding plausible fits but unstable multi-week-ahead forecasts when peak timing shifts.
proposals.rationale: Matches prior discovery pattern and surveillance note that admissions can lag an infection proxy; SEIRS supports sharp seasonal peaks via waning immunity while remaining parsimonious for a short series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is longer, forecasts may lead the observed peak (early peak timing) and underpredict the post-peak tail.
proposals.rationale: Tests a shorter reporting/admission lag while keeping the same parsimonious SEIRS backbone; can better align with rapid hospitalization onset in older adults.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Long delay can over-smooth and shift peaks too late, degrading near-term forecasts and exaggerating persistence after the peak.
proposals.rationale: Explores a longer effective lag from infection proxy to hospitalization-rate observation, which can occur with care-seeking and admission delays; retains SEIRS flexibility for high peakiness.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H dynamics may be weakly identifiable with 31 training points, causing parameter non-identifiability and unstable forecasts (especially peak height).
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the target semantics (hospitalization rate) to an explicit hospitalization compartment; can capture distinct hospitalization dynamics separate from infectious prevalence.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Mixture mapping can blur interpretation and may overfit peak magnitude by trading off I vs H contributions, reducing generalization across weeks.
proposals.rationale: Allows the observed hospitalization-rate signal to reflect a mixture of infectious burden and hospitalization occupancy/admissions proxy, potentially improving robustness when H alone is weakly identified.
